title: Learnable Learning Artifact
description: Layers 3 and 4 of the framework: the design understanding and the curriculum built on top of it. Produced by a contract-driven language model that must cite the knowledge base (kb.schema.json) or the source for every claim it makes. This is the document the viewer renders.

model.description: Model identifier that produced this artifact.

contracts.description: Contract ids and versions applied, e.g. 'lens.terraform@0.1.0'. Reproducibility depends on recording these.

openQuestions.description: Things the analyst could not establish from the evidence available. Required, not optional: a claim that cannot be cited belongs here rather than in the narrative.

Evidence.description: What a claim rests on. Either a node in the knowledge base or a location in the source, and normally both.

nodeIds.description: Node ids from kb.json. These are checkable: the linter rejects ids that do not exist.

documents.description: Repository prose the claim draws on (README, ADRs, runbooks).

method.description: Almost everything in this document is `inferred` — it is a model's reading of the system. `extracted` is reserved for values copied verbatim from the knowledge base.

contract.description: Contract id and version that produced this, e.g. 'lens.eks@0.1.0'.

Orientation.description: Lesson 1 material: what this system is for, established before any structure is described.

problem.description: The problem the system solves, in terms a non-user of it would follow. No component names.

summary.description: One paragraph. What it is, at the altitude of a whiteboard sketch.

notInScope.description: What the system deliberately does not do. Frequently more clarifying than what it does.

Lens.description: One cross-section of the system, at its own level of abstraction. Lenses are viewpoints, not directories.

question.description: The question this cross-section exists to answer, phrased as a question.

conceptIds.description: Catalog concepts a reader needs for this lens. Drives prerequisite ordering in the curriculum.

Section.description: A unit of explanation. Recursive and lazily generated: children may be present, or may be stubs naming the contract that would produce them.

kind.description: Drives which viewer component renders it. `first-principles` carries a derivation; `config-anatomy` carries annotated source; `topology` carries a diagram.

depth.description: Reading level. A lens opens at `overview`; deeper levels exist behind expansion.

body.description: Markdown. Absent when the section is an ungenerated stub.

annotatedSource.description: Required when kind is `config-anatomy`. The mechanism for teaching a workflow or manifest file, where the file itself is the subject.

expansion.description: Present when this section can be drilled into further. Its presence is what the viewer renders as an expand affordance.

Expansion.description: How to generate this section's next level of detail, on demand. Generation cost stays proportional to what is actually read.

generated.description: false means children are not yet produced; the viewer shows an expand affordance.

focus.description: What the expansion should concentrate on.

FirstPrinciples.description: The same derivation shape the concept catalog uses, applied inline to this system's specific instance of a pattern or technology.

subject.description: What is being derived, e.g. 'EKS managed control plane'.

cost.description: Mandatory. A technology taught without its cost produces cargo-culting.

whenBetter.description: The conditions under which the alternative is the better choice. Without this the comparison is an endorsement.

conceptId.description: Catalog concept this instantiates, when one exists.

AnnotatedSource.description: A source file with line-range explanations. How config-heavy domains are taught, because the file is the thing being learned.

explanation.description: What this span accomplishes and why it is needed — not a restatement of what it says.

Diagram.description: Structured diagram data. Kept as data rather than an image so the viewer can render it responsively and in either theme.

mermaid.description: Mermaid source, rendered natively by the viewer.

nodeIds.description: KB nodes depicted, so diagram elements can link to evidence.

Curriculum.description: Layer 4. An ordered path through the system, built on the lenses.

spine.description: Identifier of the lesson spine used, e.g. 'default@0.1.0'.

LessonIntent.description: The default spine's eight intents, in order. `implementation` is deliberately last.

question.description: The lesson IS a question. A lesson titled with a topic gets skimmed; a lesson titled with a question gets answered.

prerequisiteConceptIds.description: Catalog concepts assumed. The viewer offers these first if the reader has not met them.

predictProbe.description: Asked BEFORE any of the reveal is shown. Committing a wrong answer is the mechanism by which the lesson is acquired, and it is unavailable to a reader who saw the answer first.

narrative.description: Markdown. The explanation, shown after the prediction is committed.

reveal.description: What the viewer discloses once the reader has answered.

commonWrongAnswer.description: The plausible mistake, and why it is wrong. Naming it is often more instructive than the correct answer alone.

Invariant.description: Something that must always hold. Layer 3 content, and the part most likely to be violated by a future change made without understanding.

statement.description: Stated positively: what must remain true.

whyItHolds.description: The mechanism currently enforcing it — a constraint, a type, a check, or merely a convention.

enforcement.description: `convention` and `unenforced` are the interesting values: they mark invariants nothing would stop you breaking.

FailureMode.description: Lesson 5 material: what happens when a specific component fails.

failure.description: The failure, specifically: unreachable, slow, returning errors, out of disk.

effect.description: What a user observes, not what a log says.

handling.description: What the system currently does about it, including 'nothing'.

gap.description: What is not handled and would need to be.

OpenQuestion.description: Something the analyst could not determine. Emitting these is mandatory: it is where a claim goes when it cannot be cited, and it is what keeps the narrative trustworthy.

wouldResolveIf.description: What would answer it — the file, the person, or the measurement needed.
